Alpha slides the loss from SSIM to silhouette

score = 0.30 · SSIM(tone & structure)  +  0.70 · Silhouette(1 − stray ink / N)
alpha 0 — pure SSIM, matches tone, edges fizz alpha 1 — pure silhouette, clean edges, flat tone

Both terms score every candidate glyph in the chosen set against every cell. SSIM asks whether the glyph's tone and structure match the patch; it cannot tell ink on the subject from ink hanging into empty paper. Silhouette asks only that the glyph not ink where the patch is blank. Alpha is the convex weight between them — it was called white_weight in greedyIOU.

Two honest limits. rembg is a 176 MB ONNX model and cannot run in a browser, so the cabbage ships with its background already removed by the Python pipeline. The five sculptures are bundled as supplied — they arrive isolated on white already, and a matte made two of them worse. An upload is scored as given, background and all; run python -m ascii_SSIM.cutout first if that matters.

Downscaling here uses canvas resampling rather than the LANCZOS filter convert.py uses, so a render may differ from the Python pipeline by a few cells. The glyph rasters, the equalization LUT, the percentile threshold and the scoring are ports of the Python, not approximations of it.
